# Olympus

**The whole Olympus army in one window, inside World of Warcraft: Forever.**

Olympus is Asmongold's guild for *World of Warcraft: Forever*: Alliance, PvP ruleset, a
place to find dungeon groups, organize raids, share class knowledge and build the guild
together. It grew past **10,000 members during the beta**. A WoW guild caps at 1,000
members, so Olympus is really a *realm* of many Olympus guilds. In game each player
only ever sees the roster of their own guild. Nobody could tell how many Olympus guilds
exist, who leads them, or where the army is.

This addon answers exactly that. It adds up every Olympus guild live, in a window that
looks like Blizzard's Guild window and docks right next to it.

![The whole army at a glance: every Olympus guild, live](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dnl-gentile/olympus-addon/main/docs/olympus-1.jpg)

![The Realm: the King, the Treasurer and every Lord and Captain](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dnl-gentile/olympus-addon/main/docs/olympus-2.jpg)

![Every guild in detail: hover a guild for members, online, Lord, free slots, level and classes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dnl-gentile/olympus-addon/main/docs/olympus-3.jpg)

![One click to anyone: whisper, invite or find a Lord or Captain](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dnl-gentile/olympus-addon/main/docs/olympus-4.jpg)

![Where the army stands: soldiers per zone on the world map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dnl-gentile/olympus-addon/main/docs/olympus-5.jpg)

> **Status:** built for WoW: Forever and running on the Forever beta (1.60.1), where the
> census already adds up reports from many Olympus guilds. Also tested on Classic Era (1.15)
> and Anniversary (2.5). Please report anything that looks wrong (`/oly bug`).

---

**Horde too.** Olympus guilds on the Horde side use the same addon. The factions can't see
each other's guilds, so each one gets its own census, channels, decrees and untabarded list: the
addon picks yours from your character. On the Horde, the Crown is every Horde Olympus guild
master and the officers of the Horde guild named exactly "Olympus", if there is one.

## Who can use it

**Only members of a guild with "Olympus" in its name**, however it was spelled: OLYMPVS the Roman way, Olimpus, Olmps, Olympuz, Olympos, Olimpo and other misspellings count too (Olympia or Olympic do not), and a guild against Olympus ("ANTI OLYMPUS", "Olympus Haters") does not, nor (1.6.0) one that names Olympus only to measure itself against it or to say it is not Olympus ("Stronger Than Olympus", "Not Even Olympus"). The check is fixed in the code and
cannot be switched off with a command. Outside an Olympus guild the addon joins no channel
and hears nothing of the army, but for the author's signed list below, over its own guild.
The only thing it offers there is the **Join Olympus**
screen described below, and its own few addon whispers are the only ones it sends or hears
there (which guild to ask, the answer, and your request, each to or from the one member
concerned).

**And only after accepting the Olympus Accord**, Olympus's terms of use, once per game
account: until then the addon sends and hears nothing of the army, in an Olympus guild too, and
its window shows the Accord alone (see [Privacy](#privacy)).

**Approved guilds (1.1).** A guild of Asmon's Olympus whose name the rule leaves out (it leaves
Olympian and Olympia out on purpose) counts as an Olympus guild once the author names it in his
signed list: the same list, signed with the same key on his own computer, that names the High
Council and the King's Steward, for one faction and realm group. No census vote counts, and nobody
else can add one. A few ship with the addon itself, so their members have nothing to paste: since
1.1, the Alliance's `<OLYMPIAN>`, and since 1.1.5 its `<OLYMPIANS>` too (only a new version takes one of those off). Its members' addons, no Olympus members
until they hold that list, take it over their own guild alone (the list only: nothing else is
read, and they send nothing). The first of them pastes it with `/oly approved paste`, or a click
on the Join Olympus screen's last line (the author
or a High Councillor hands out the signed text; it is checked like any list, so it can't be forged
or changed), and his addon passes it to his guild every 5 minutes. `/oly approved` lists the
approved guilds of your faction. A newer signed list without a guild ends it on every client.

**Removed guilds (1.1.5).** A guild the High Council removed from Olympus is no Olympus guild,
whatever its name: its census, chats and marks are gone and its members' addon shows the Join
Olympus screen. Its way back is an appeal to the council: once the author names it in his signed
approved list, it counts again, with no new version. Until a player updates, the council's
[net-off](#net-off-11-the-moderators-hide-a-character-or-take-a-guild-off-the-network) word takes
such a guild off the network live.

**Guild verification (launch).** A guild's guild master verifies it once, with a verifier: the King,
a High Councillor of the signed list or the author. Each Olympus guild has a 7-day clock from its
start: the first time a verifier's client saw it, the same on every client (each client keeps the
earliest start a verifier's client gave, so a reinstall, a rejoin or a new guild master never
restarts it; until one reaches it, a client counts from its own first sighting). 1.5.4 started every
guild's clock again on its release night (2026-11-09, 00:00 Brasília time): a guild seen before
then has its 7 days from that moment (the grace was 48 hours before 1.5.4). Meanwhile its guild
master sees **GM verification pending** (once a session, and the line on top of the Census or
`/oly verify` opens it again) with the steps: whisper a verifier (**Whisper a verifier** writes it
for him in Olympus's own whisper window, with a short code), or **Resend verification request**
to an available High Councillor. Resending keeps the original deadline, including after a reload;
an accepted request has a five-minute cooldown, and only the councillor's acknowledgement confirms
receipt. If nobody is available or the local queue refuses it, the button can be tried again. A verifier
approves it from The Watch's **Guilds** (every Olympus guild still to verify, with its guild master,
members, time left and code, overdue ones first; a click approves it or whispers its guild master,
who may not have the addon yet; **Copy the list** opens it in a window to copy from) or with
`/oly verify approve <Guild> [Guild master]` or `<code>`; `/oly verify revoke <Guild>` takes one
back, even where the verifier's own client never received that approval (1.6.0: the guild master's name
follows the guild's only when the census doesn't know it; a name that isn't the guild master known there
sends nothing, as it may be the end of another guild's name). A revocation takes the guild's check off every
client that receives it; a guild the moderators take off the network shows no check either, but its
approval stands until a verifier revokes it. To take its verification back as well, revoke it first:
a week off the network leaves no census row to name it, and then only a verifier whose client holds its
approval (the one who approved it, for one) or still lists it in The Watch can revoke it. The verifiers are told once of each pending guild (and
of each new guild master to check) and reminded 12 hours before its deadline. A verification belongs to the guild **and** its guild
master: while the census names someone else as guild master, it lapses until the new one is
verified, on the guild's same clock. Past its 7 days an unverified guild is overdue. Member-facing popups, chat warnings and Census
notices are temporarily paused; 1.6.2 also pauses the automatic guild-master reminders and attention banners. Manual verification and resending remain available. (1.6.0.1) On WoW: Forever's PvP, RP
and RP-PvP realms every guild waits, pending, until 30 November 2026 (`Verify.OTHER_GROUPS_WAIT_UNTIL`), with nothing asked
of its guild master and nothing overdue; an approval still verifies, and from then each unverified guild there has its 7 days.
The guild stays on the verifiers' list, marked overdue; and its guild master's own
powers in Olympus wait for his verification (others take him as an officer: his public card, his
Legates and correspondents, his guild decrees and his guild bank grant wait too). Nothing is taken
from the members and nobody is removed. The King's guild needs none. Verified guilds carry a mark
in the Census (an overdue one, for the verifiers); the King's guild carries the verified mark too
(1.5.9), whoever its guild master is. Being verified grants no role or council
status. Switches in `Core.lua`: `ns.VERIFY_HOLD` (the guild master's hold, on) and
`ns.VERIFY_GATE` (the older overdue-guild gate through `ns.GuildSanctioned`, off). Forever shared-tools participation uses existing approvals through [FederationProgram](https://github.com/dnl-gentile/olympus-addon/blob/main/docs/FEDERATION-PROGRAM.md), independently of that older switch; the
exemptions are one predicate, `Verify.Exempt`.

Verification catch-up crosses signed relays to an available verifier without sending requests to
every guild. It compares the contents of saved decisions as well as their counts, and recovers an
approval with its original verifier and date; rebuilding census rows does not erase that decision.
In **The Watch → Guilds → Verified guilds**, click a guild and choose **Resend approval** to send
the one decision already held, with the original verifier, guild master and date. It doesn't
restart verification or the grace period. A newer decision takes precedence. On Forever an updated
relay forwards the resend to the named guild's reporter through the existing verification route.
From 1.6.0 on Forever a guild master's own guild also hands him its approval: a guildmate whose
client holds it from a verifier, naming the guild master the census shows now, sends that one
decision over guild chat as the resend does (its original verifier and date: nothing is approved
anew). It goes when his client asks (with its verification ask, while the guild shows unverified
there, and again when a guildmate on 1.6.0 comes online) and, to a guild master on an older
version, at his login and about every half hour while he plays; a guild gets one every 5 minutes
at most, and none from a client in quiet presence. A guildmate whose newest decision on the guild
is a newer revocation answers such a hand-over, or the ask, with that revocation. So a new
installation, or an approval given while he was away, no longer leaves him on **GM verification
pending** while a guildmate who holds it is online, even with no verifier online. A 1.5.9 client
that takes a hand-over counts it as the answer to its own verification ask and skips its login's
retry: it receives the other guilds' decisions at its next half-hourly ask (or sooner, from a
guildmate's answered ask handed to the guild).
Guild rows in The Watch open actions to review verification, copy the exact spelling, or hide
the row and its verifier reminders on this installation. **Manage hidden guilds** restores a row.
**Check current guild master** requests a fresh native roster scan from this client for its own
guild, or privately from one recently heard reporter for another guild. The result names its
source and stays informational. An older client, an offline reporter or an incomplete roster can
leave the poll unanswered.
A missing local record still needs a valid verifier's copy. A member's claimed approver name, an
old census total or a guild-start clock cannot create an approval, and an older approval cannot
replace a retained revocation.

### Not in Olympus yet?
First it asks the obvious question: *"? Disband immediately. What are you
doing?"* If you are in no guild, Olympus opens the **Join Olympus** page on your first login
with the addon. **Request to join** searches for an online Olympus member and opens a request
you can edit. Click **Send** to whisper it. The screen waits 45 seconds before offering
**Request again** with another contact. If you enable reminders, the same prompt appears
when the 45 seconds expire, even if you received a whisper reply or closed the Join page.
Confirm to prepare a new request. **Browse Olympus guilds** opens the optional guild list.

From 1.6.0, after the guild of the King's gates (where one of its own whose answer says he recruits
comes first), the screen asks a member whose own answer says he recruits, then the Lords, Captains
and recruiters the answers name, and only then anyone else `/who` found. Each click also asks the
addons of the members it would ask next, together (4 a click at most, each once): a click's request
opens at once and their answers choose the next one. When the screen opens a request on its own,
after a search or when the member it chose can't take it, it waits for those answers (3 seconds at
most) and asks first one whose answer says he recruits. An answer counts for 10 minutes: a member
whose answer is older is asked again before a request to him opens. A member whose answer says he
can't invite (no invite right, or a full guild) is passed over before you write to him; a request
already open for him closes with a line saying why, and the next member is asked. When the request
already went, the wait ends as soon as you may send another and the screen says why (the reminder,
when on, comes then). When the member asked recruits, the screen says your request goes to his
invite queue while his 45 seconds run. When nobody is left to ask, the screen says so (every guild
found full, or everyone found already asked or unable to take the request). Once everyone found was
asked, **Request again** searches with `/who` first: a member who logged in since is asked before
anyone else, and a member asked 10 minutes ago or more is asked again only when that search found
nobody new. Members on versions before 1.6.0 say nothing of themselves, and are asked as before.

The list uses the game's own `/who`, which returns up to 50 players per search. When there
are more, each new click searches a range of levels and adds to the list. Replies are
highlighted. Olympus uses its own editable confirmation window in both input modes.

**Where to go**: a search also asks one member's addon (an addon whisper, not a chat line) where
recruits should go, and its census answers: the guild the King opened **the gates** of first,
then the guilds with the **most free slots**, and a couple of their Lords and Captains online
(never the King). From 1.6.0 the answer also says whether a request pops up for that member now,
waits in his list or can't be taken (no invite right, or a full guild), and names first his own
guild's members who recruit (himself while his recruiting is on and no instance, chat lockdown or
pause holds his pop-ups, then those whose hello says they take handoffs). It names only what the census confirms: guilds two members' reports agree on, and
Lords and Captains two reports name. The screen lists them in that order, each once `/who` found
one of its members (the gates once a second member's answer agrees: one more is asked), the
guilds found with `/who` too, and a click asks one of that guild's recruiters (from 1.6.0) or
officers that `/who` found in it, or another member it found there. Just before, their addon is
asked whether they take recruit whispers (again if it never answered). A member who set **do not contact** (`/oly
nocontact on`) is never offered, however many recruits ask him, and the question closes before
anything is sent. It stays **one whisper per click**, in your own words (no dues line), 20
seconds apart. With it goes your request to the same member, so an officer's addon shows it with
**Invite** and **Decline** instead of a raw whisper; one who recruits by whisper (1.5.9) gets it
as a **JOIN**: the invite pop-up opens by itself, unless he chose **Queue only**. Members on
versions before 1.1 just get the whisper, as before.

**A guild's public charter.** On the Realm, **Your guild's public charter** lets its current
guild master publish a short purpose (48 bytes), client language, raid nights (24 bytes), and
wanted classes. Each edit renews the card for seven days, and so does his addon's repeat
while he plays, so it lasts seven days after he last played; an edit keeps the card's other fields
whatever its age; members keep the cards they heard across a `/reload`. Withdrawing it publishes
an empty card. Receiving members accept it only from the current guild master under the same
roster or census/signed-authority checks as other guild-master powers. Losing that authority or
letting the card expire removes it. Public words use the game's logged addon messages.
The same Realm page lists known sister-guild cards. **Write to this guild's Lord...** opens
an editable letter for the member to send; a transfer remains a conversation and the destination
officer's manual invitation, with no automatic removal from the member's current guild.

Under **Church → Invites**, a guild master can ask the Apostles for help with recruiting.
The request shares the guild name, faction and time with the Olympus network in that ruleset
for 24 hours. The guild master can withdraw it. An Apostle can open an editable whisper to
the current guild master and choose whether to send it.

The Join screen can request at most three cards from each queried member, with at most three
queried members. Two distinct queried members must report the exact same author, revision and
card before it helps routing; a conflicting or missing card gives no affinity. This is a
corroborated report, not proof of unique people or a new authority to invite. The King's
confirmed open gates still come first; next come matching client language, a wanted class,
and an optional friend found by `/who` here, in that order, then free slots. The
friend's name is a local preference chosen on the Join screen and is never sent. The route
still contacts only a member `/who` found here, one manual whisper per click, and
officers still use the game's manual invitation. Older addons ignore the versioned charter
messages and keep their ordinary Join routing. The two factions use separate cards and
channels; the same charter and Join controls work for each side.

## What it does

### Census: the army at a glance
- Every Olympus guild in one list: **Guild · Members · Online · Avg lvl · Lord**. Columns sort by
  clicking, like the Guild window: a first click on Members, Online or Avg lvl puts the highest
  first, a second the lowest. By default, fresh reports and larger guilds come first; at the same
  size the exact `<OLYMPUS>` comes first, then the higher average level, then the name.
  Any other column's tie, whichever way it runs, goes to the exact `<OLYMPUS>` first, then the
  higher average level, then the name; by Avg lvl, a guild without one comes last either way and
  a tie goes to `<OLYMPUS>`, then the larger guild. A title wider than its column (the
  narrow window, a longer language's words) shows its short form (*Memb.*, *Onl.*, *Avg*), or is
  cut with "..." inside its own header, never over the next one.
- The Realm lists its guilds in the same default order, and its own **Order** line above them
  sorts them by members (the default), online, average level, guild or Lord: a count the
  highest first, a name A to Z, ties as in the Census. A column clicked in the Census leaves the
  Realm as it was, and the Realm's order leaves the Census as it was.
- **Avg lvl**: each guild's average level from its report, to the tenth and cut down as
  the report carries it, your own guild's too, so every client shows the same number (`-` when a
  report carries none, as an older version's, or one no guild can have). The Realm shows it in
  parentheses after each Lord's *online* or *offline*, Recruiting after each guild's free slots,
  and the copy for Discord in a column of its own. Wherever guilds are listed by a count (free
  slots, soldiers in a zone, a map pin, the Royal Inspection, the dues table after its members),
  the same count goes to the exact `<OLYMPUS>` first, then the higher average level, then the
  name, and the average level shows after the count (in the dues table, in each guild's hover).
- **Total soldiers** and **online now** across the whole realm. The current server's soldiers stay prominent; the smaller **all servers** total includes accepted observations
  from the other supported realm groups. People estimates remain inside the details page. Stored
  observations retain their original time and are shown while the current census rebuilds.
  Scoped snapshots restore a new client's count immediately. Complete, newer coverage may raise
  or lower it. Legacy caches that lost their PvE/PvP origin are preserved separately and labelled
  as excluded, without clearing guild verification or its deadline. A complete set of correctly
  scoped direct reports can substantiate an existing saved view. While no newer report of another
  guild reaches your addon, the saved count stays past its day instead of losing a guild at a time
  (1.6.0): the header's hover says why, the **all servers** total gives the date of its oldest part
  once that is more than a day old (*8,726 all servers (as of 05/17)*), the census page shows the
  saved count's date (**This server as of**) and `/oly bug`'s census line marks it *saved*, with its
  age. Once anything newer arrives, a guild unheard for a day leaves the count as before.
- **The census in numbers**: a click on the header's count (from any tab) opens a page of its own
  in the Census tab: characters, people, linked alts, online now, the guilds counted (and how many
  report right now), the army's average level (each guild's, weighted by its size), every server
  (the characters and people of all of them, by ruleset, by region and by faction, then each
  server, yours first; another server's numbers arrive through players who also play there, counted
  when it is what you saw yourself, when two players agree, when a moderator says it or (1.5.5) when
  the addon's author does, and listed grey otherwise; the beta's realms never count) and the levels
  online. Forwarded observations preserve the original observer and date across normal members and
  reloads. Repeating the same original through several holders never creates independent
  witnesses. Without authenticated original evidence, these foreign counts are visible as reports,
  outside the accepted total; the one portable proof is the author's own look signed with his
  account key (1.5.5), which counts whoever carries it. A family shared across regions
  has an unknown aggregate region; the relay's location is not assigned to all its members.
  An ordinary carrier sends the complete aggregate in one logical chunk, with only the whole
  guild-detail rows that fit beside it. The local scoped snapshot sends at most 180 guild rows
  per packet; a larger local census needs subsequent reconciliation for the remaining rows.
  Two small graphs show how the
  counts moved: the characters over the last 30 days (each day's highest) and who was online over
  the last 24 hours (each hour's most); hover a day or an hour for its numbers. Your own addon
  writes the census down every 15 minutes while you play, about 3 minutes after login once the
  census is rebuilt, and keeps 30 days of it in your saved variables (the last two days sample by
  sample). Nothing is sent: another player's client keeps its own history, so the curves can
  differ. **< The Census**, or any tab, goes back to the list.
- **Where the army stands**: top zones ("Stormwind City 742") and totals per continent
  (Eastern Kingdoms, Kalimdor), counted by the guilds whose census comes from a member who
  shares their zone (see Privacy, below).
- Hover a guild: members, online, free slots, average level, inactive members, classes online, top zones.
- **Right after login** the header, the Census and the Realm say *Rebuilding the census
  after login: N guilds heard so far* for about 3 minutes, while every guild's reporter answers.
  The beta often loads an empty save. The army is not gone, and no `/reload` is needed. The line
  only waits: it asks nothing (no `/who`) and opens nothing.
- **An update line**: when the author's own addon says on the Olympus channel that a newer
  version than yours is out (he marks it once CurseForge lists it, never a build he is still
  trying), a line at the foot of the Census, one line in chat once a session and `/oly status`
  say so. It is yours alone: nothing is sent and nobody is whispered.
- **Marked rows**: a warning mark on a guild whose senders disagree (on its Lord or
  Captains, or on its size, by more than 5 members or 5% plus the 20 a minute a guild may gain or
  lose between their two reports), a question mark on one that a single
  sender stands behind. Its tooltip says which and who: check before calling a muster or opening
  the gates on it (the gates ask again, with the reason). A marked row can still be right, and
  the mark changes nothing that counts. Your own guild (your roster) is never marked.
- **Asking to join**: a recruit who asked you from the Join Olympus screen shows on top of
  the Census, with their whisper. An officer (the game's guild invite permission) answers with
  **Invite** (the game's own guild invite) or **Decline** (one whisper pointing to the gates'
  guild while the King's gates are open, else naming your guild alone: never a guild the census
  lists for its room, which two made-up characters could report), one click each; anyone else
  can point them to an officer online. **Dismiss** sends nothing. While you recruit by whisper
  (1.5.9), a request goes to **Church → Invites** instead and is taken as a **JOIN**: the same
  invite pop-up, unless you chose **Queue only**; turning recruiting off brings it back here. In the Realm's Recruiting, one
  click (or `/oly nocontact`) sets your **do not contact** flag.
- **Search the census**: a guild, a Lord, a Captain, a player of a guild's top five or one
  seen online (the player shows under the guild's row), or a zone ("Stormwind": its soldiers
  and its guilds, most first). Type **recruiting** (or `free 50`) for every guild with room,
  most free slots first and the King's gates on top. Letters that look alike count as one:
  l, I and 1, and 0 and O, so `XIII` finds OLYMPUS XIlI. The Realm tab's search reads
  its guilds, Lords, Captains and members seen, and its classes, races and professions, the
  same way.
- **Tonight on this computer**: under the list, the most soldiers your addon saw online at
  once tonight and when, and (in its tooltip, and next to a zone you search) how each zone
  filled or emptied since. Counted by your own addon once a minute from the reports it
  already holds, starting about 3 minutes after login once the census is rebuilt. Another
  player's client counts its own evening, and nothing is sent.
- **The sanitized census** (for the census statistics and the Companion): banned guilds (taken
  off the network) apart at their last size heard, departed guilds (not heard for 24 hours), how sure
  each guild's size is (our roster, confirmed by two reporters or more, relayed, one reporter,
  disputed, older report), and a size that jumps past what a guild can do held at its last good size
  until two reporters agree. Worked out from the reports your addon already holds; it keeps each
  guild's last good size for 7 days in its SavedVariables and sends nothing. The header's count is
  not changed by it. The definition is `docs/CENSUS-STATS.md`.
- Olympus guilds where nobody runs the addon show too, in grey: opening the window (and any click in it) also searches
  `/who` and lists every Olympus guild it sees online, with how many. They count in no total.

### The Realm: the hierarchy
- **War Room**: every Olympus member can read their guild's operations, Centuries and after-action
  records (a record stays its 90 days after its operation goes, 30 days after it closed,
  listed under the earlier operations' reports), declare their own accepted roles, post an LFG
  card and answer an operation's invitation.
  The guild master, Captains, its confirmed War correspondent and signed War councillors who are
  in that same guild manage its operations and records. A councillor of another guild gets no
  cross-guild writing power. Its military groups (up to 25, each an appointed Legate and up to
  39 guildmates, 40 people total) have explicit appointments in every guild, including the King's.
  A Legate manages their own agreed group; existing authorized officers retain oversight.
  Guilds, Classes and Races remain views of known census information
  available to members, not privileged command consoles. Empty lists say what is missing, and a
  role preview sends no War Room action.
- Below Search in the light header, **Guilds / Classes / Races / Professions** select four views of the
  same known people. Guilds keeps the hierarchy below. The other views group into collapsible
  sections and sort each group by level, then name. Rows show the known guild and guild rank;
  an operational role appears only after the player or an authorized officer actually records
  one. Your guild comes from your live roster. Other guilds are partial (their reports and
  players seen with `/who`). Race comes from your live roster or `/who` result when the client
  directly exposes it, or from a consented Arena profile; these local observations do not add a
  race field to census reports. A race a `/who` answer showed stays known for the rest of the
  session, after its round is over or the player logs off (in memory only, never saved or sent,
  gone at a reload and with `/oly reset`). The Races view's **Unknown** group says on hover where a
  race comes from. Profession skill/current cap comes from the crafter's consented
  listing with its age. Unknown data stays
  **Unknown**. Olympus does not infer a role from class or pretend another player's professions
  came from inspect. Each view keeps its own search and collapsed groups for the session.
- The **King**, then every guild's **Lord** (guild master) and **Captains** (the officer rank
  right below the guild master).
  Each shows level, class and online or *offline 3d*. Long absences show in red
  (`/oly warndays <days>`, 3 by default). **A Lord away**: when a Lord crosses that, one
  chat line, once per absence. It goes to his own guild's officers from their roster, and to the King,
  his Steward and his Hands for every guild's Lord, by the census's word (a guild that stopped
  reporting included, counted from its last report even when that showed him online). Never a
  popup, and nothing is done to anyone.
- The **Treasurer of Olympus** (Pyralis Ashandar, chosen by Asmongold's chat) right under
  the King, with a gold coin next to his name wherever he shows, his tooltip and his lines in
  the Olympus chats included. Only
  that exact character of the guild OLYMPUS gets it: look-alikes don't.
- **Members online** under each guild: your own guild's from your roster, any other's from
  `/who`. Opening a guild searches `/who` for that guild alone (up to 50 of its players).
  Click a name to whisper, invite or `/who` them.
- The **ranks** of each guild with how many members hold them.
- **Inactive members**: offline 7+ and 30+ days, per guild. Your own guild's line (or
  `/oly inactive`) opens the list by name: members offline 7, 14 or 30 days and more,
  with rank, class, level and last online, from your own roster, longest away first. A rank
  that may remove members (as in the game's Guild window: ranks below yours) removes **one
  person per click**, after a question that shows their rank and days away, a few seconds
  apart. There is no kick-all, and nothing is sent.
- **Mentors**: a Lord opens **Recruits and their mentors** on that page (or `/oly recruits`):
  his guild's lowest rank and whoever joined since he logged in. He clicks a recruit who is
  online, then one of his Captains, and says yes: **one whisper to each** from that click, the
  Captain told who to look after, the recruit told who to ask. The pair shows on his list (his
  client's alone); nothing goes on the channel.
- **Legates and correspondents**: a guild master of an Olympus guild (not the King's)
  has a tab of his own in the Throne's place, **Guild** (or `/oly nominees`), laid out as the
  King's Hands page: **+ Name a legate** (his target, or a name he types), his list (a click
  takes a title back, asked first), and a line per High Council department to name its
  correspondent. Up to 25
  Legates and one correspondent per department (6 at most), members of his own guild only: the
  addon refuses a 26th Legate, a second correspondent for a department, one name twice and
  anyone outside his roster, and says why. By decision of the High Council, Legates and
  correspondents no longer receive the bronze dragon frame merely for their office: a Legate gets
  the Legate shield and a correspondent gets their department's shield. A signed High Councillor
  likewise gets their department shield without replacing the Council's silver frame. Earned
  honours remain round the portrait underneath the separate badge. Offices count only while
  verified in the guild. Existing appointees receive this explanation once; a real office or
  department change explains the new badge again.
  His own client sends the list on the Olympus channel; every addon takes it from that guild's
  master alone (proven as for his bronze wings: your roster for your own guild, two census senders
  for another), retains accepted bounded lists across logouts and offline periods, and drops the
  duty when a verified removal or change of guild master is seen. `/oly nominees legate <name>`
  (the old `centurion` spelling remains an alias), `/oly nominees correspondent
   ` and `/oly nominees remove ` do it in chat.
  A confirmed correspondent also sees a **Guild** workspace for their own department. War and
  Justice duties apply only to their own guild, checked against its fresh roster and its current
  guild master's nomination; neither title grants federal powers. Artisanry links to its existing
  board and says its dedicated workflow is not available yet. Heraldry runs its own guild's
  Decrees, Agenda and musters; its current appointment grants no global Crown authority. A Church
  contact still needs a Church appointment for its private room and recruitment numbers.
  A Legate organizes an agreed raid group of 40 including themselves (up to 39 guildmates),
  coordinating attendance at events, raids and wars. Groups are optional and fluid, not exclusive
  partitions or restrictions on playing with another leader when theirs is offline. The appointed
  character receives a quiet
  explanation once per appointment. They can edit their own group's list, not another leader's;
  existing authorized officers retain oversight. Old oversized saved groups stay read-only until
  an authorized, confirmed replacement archives the original membership privately. No guild
  invitations, removals or native promotions happen automatically. An online member of the group
  has **Invite online member to raid**: one party invite on the Legate's click, only while
  the guild roster still lists that member.
- **Top levels**: the highest level players of the realm.
- **Recruiting**: the guilds that still have free slots, so new players go where there is room
  (the five with the most, then every one on a click).
  When the King opens **the gates** of a guild, it tops the list: send new recruits there.
- **Layers** of your zone, named after the highest ranked Olympus member on each one
  ("Asmongold's layer"), with how many members are there.

### Layer hop: join the King's layer without begging in chat
While Asmongold is online, the top of the Census and the Realm shows **"Ask invite for Asmon
Layer"** with his crown. One click (or `/oly hop`) and the addon does the asking:

- You must already be in his zone (a layer is read per zone). If you are not, the line says
  where he is and nothing is asked.
- It asks the Olympus players on his layer who can invite (alone, or leading a group with a
  free seat). Only a handful answer, picked at random on each player's side, so a crowd of
  askers is spread over many players instead of flooding one.
- It picks one of them, favouring players outside a group and with fewer recent invites. They
  get **"X wants to join your layer"** with **Invite**, **Not now** and **Always invite**. No
  answer or a no, and the next one is asked. **Always invite** invites the next ones without
  the window while that player is alone or with only the addon's hop guests; clicked while they
  lead a party or raid of their own, it also covers that group until it ends (GitHub
  issue #50). That group's permission is never
  saved: a later group asks first again, after a `/reload` the window asks once more, and
  `/oly layerauto off` ends it at once.
- The invite is accepted for you when that player is one the addon can vouch for (a member of
  your own guild, the King, his Steward or Hands, or, once the author's signed list is on, a Lord
  or Captain of `<Olympus>` it names; never a census rank); anyone else's, and every invite
  while Blizzard's gamepad UI is on, waits for your click in the game's own invite window. The
  game moves you to the layer, and the addon takes you out of the group as soon as it sees the
  move (or offers a **Leave group** button if it can't tell).

Players alone on the King's layer are asked once per login: **"Asmon is online and you are on
his layer. May the addon invite the players who want to join, and take them out of the group
once they are there?"** with **For Olympus!**, **Can't right now** and **Invite manually**, and
a **Don't ask me again** box. With For Olympus! the addon invites on its own (only while you
are alone or with its guests, never into a group of your friends) and lets each guest go after
90 seconds. The guest's addon leaves the group, since only a click may remove someone.

Any other layer in the Realm tab's layer list works the same way: click it. Everyone who
shares their zone and layer (`/oly location on`) and said yes to layer help (the
first-open page, or `/oly layerhelp on`) helps. A player who keeps them private is never asked, since an offer would tell the asker where they are. `/oly layerhelp
off` stops the requests, `/oly layerhelp on` also forgets the answer to the King's layer
window, `/oly layerauto on` invites them without the window. Helpers must be in the same zone
as the layer they are on, and the King himself is never asked.

On Forever, if nobody in your guild offers to help, Olympus can ask up to three known members
of sister guilds who recently shared the selected layer on your sub-realm. Both clients must
recognize each other's Olympus membership. Helpers still need to opt in to location sharing
and layer help, and both players confirm the group invitation by hand.

Layers are known from the members who share their zone and layer (see Privacy, below):
the more share, the better hopping works. Asking works either way, and says on the channel
the zone you are in and the layer you want. If the King's own layer announcement has not
arrived yet, clicking his hop line sends one discovery question on the Olympus channel while his crown is visible.
Clients that can see his exact nameplate keep that fact private until the question; eligible
helpers answer the asker alone, and two independent answers must agree before the ordinary
layer-hop ask begins. A lone or conflicting answer moves nobody. Turning location sharing,
layer help or the crown off cancels a queued answer and privately withdraws one already sent
while that discovery question remains active.

The King's layer is known only while his crown
shows on the map (**Show me on the map** on his Throne, off by default): his addon sends it
the moment he shows the crown and repeats it every minute while it shows. With his crown
hidden (or while he is in a dungeon, where it hides) the line says so instead of "try again in
a minute". A layer is a copy of a zone inside one realm: when the census places him on another
realm than yours, the line says that, even if his layer reaches your channel. The `king:` line
of `/oly status` (and of `/oly bug`) says what your addon knows of him: online and how sure,
his realm, his layer and his crown, and how long ago each was heard.

**On WoW: Forever (1.5.4, experimental).** Forever splits a realm group into sub-realms, and a
group invite alone does not move you between them. The request goes to your own guild. A layer
can be listed even when no guildmate there has enabled location sharing and layer help, or can
invite you at that moment. A guildmate's layer on another sub-realm is
listed apart from a same-numbered layer on yours, with that server's label (`[Realm5]`), and
asking for it works the same up to the group: once you are in the helper's group, Olympus tells
you to log out to the character screen and back in (the others' portraits show dark blue until
then, as you are not with them yet), and to close the game and open it again if that was not enough.
The pending hop is kept in your saved variables for 15 minutes: back in the game, in the helper's
group and on his server, the usual confirmation (two different NPCs on the layer) and the leave
finish it; still on your old server, one line says to restart; out of the group, or 15 minutes
later, the hop ends with a line and your group is left alone. The helper's addon keeps such a
guest 15 minutes instead of 90 seconds, and his window says the guest arrives after a relog. Every
hop entry point is marked experimental, and the first ask of a session (for a layer here, and for
one on another server) shows the whole flow first, with **Ask** and **Cancel**. `/oly hop
@` asks for a listed layer on another server; `/oly hop status` shows the pending hop.

### Party Guard
While the King is online, clear whispers asking for a party invite can appear in the Census
(`/oly partyguard on | off`). The whisper is only a request, never proof of guild membership.
Party Guard labels it only from a fresh guild roster, that exact player as your target or
mouseover, or a new name `/who` result requested from the row after the whisper. It ignores older
cached `/who` results, never invites automatically and requires an extra confirmation for someone
verified outside Olympus. Someone you invited from Party Guard, or who is already in your group, makes
no new request for 30 minutes; after that, his whisper is a request again.

### Person details
Click any Lord, Captain, racer or inspected player. Their profile opens in the Olympus window, at
its size, with the census facts Olympus knows: level, class, zone, rank and status. **Back**
returns to the same list or Realm subpage, one opened from another first; **Whisper**,
**Invite** and **Who** stay on it (offline: **Who** alone). It is not the Blood Arena
companion's profile, and opening it sends no query. `/oly profile Name` (or `Name-Realm`) opens
one by name. Yours is **My profile** (`/oly profile`, the Realm, the Games tab, the Games
window's **Edit my profile**): **Look** (frame, title, nickname, emblem; one not released yet in
grey), **Icons**, **Who sees what**, **Letters** (the King's), and you as others see you.
Any soldier can reach the Lord of another Olympus guild in two clicks.

A High Councillor's tooltip says so too: their mark and own icon after their name, then
**High Councillor**, their department and their title, for whoever may see the council (the
same as their card); none on the King's screen while the council's names are hidden.

**Player tooltips** (your own portrait's Olympus menu) adds a compact guild and rank
line for Olympus players when the game supplies the rank. Its own settings panel can turn
that line or its class colour off and adjust player-tooltip size from 80% to 140% (100% by
default). Native text, owner and positioning stay with the game; no other tooltip addon is
required. These additions pause during combat and with the gamepad UI. The original size
returns when the tooltip clears, hides, combat begins or the input mode changes; a later size
change by another addon is preserved. Secret ranks and covered or hidden council identities
are not exposed. The compact presentation takes inspiration from
[PrettyTooltip](https://github.com/FallenShard/PrettyTooltip); no third-party code or assets
are bundled.

### Right-click a player (1.1.2)
Right-click a player (the target frame, party and raid frames, a name in chat, the Who list, the
friends list, a community roster) and the game's menu gets an **Olympus** part at the bottom:
- **Their version**: "Olympus 1.1.1 (out of date)", "up to date" or "not seen yet", and under it
  where it came from and when. Guildmates are listed without asking (their addon says hello to
  your guild), and so is a known version on the person card. Opening the menu sends nothing.
- **Check version**: for anyone else, one tiny addon whisper that their addon answers with its
  version and nothing else (a player once every 2 minutes, 6 a minute). Only 1.1.2 and newer
  answer, so no answer in 10 seconds can mean no Olympus, an older one, a dungeon or raid, or no
  Olympus guild (outside one the addon sends nothing). The author's check is his roll call to that
  player alone, which every version since 0.9.9 answers, and only after their yes to his roll calls.
- **Ask to update** (1.2.1: the author, the King and the High Council only; others' asks are
  dropped), when they are behind the newest version your addon knows. Nothing goes before
  you confirm. On 1.1.2 or newer their addon shows a compact notice with both versions and where to
  update; **Read update** opens a plain-language parchment letter: reviewed public release notes
  and the safe next step. For an older one, confirming opens a whisper you send with the ask. One
  ask per player a day, 5 an hour;
  they see one a day at most, **Don't remind me** hides them for 7 days (on the beta
  they last until you log out), and a player they block (`/oly block`) or
  ignore, or one the moderators took off, never gets through. The notice never names a version the
  author has not released. The author's pick sends his usual update window, naming the version he
  marked as out (`/oly released`).
- **Tell them about Olympus**, when their addon did not answer: a whisper with a short invite and
  the CurseForge link (to get it, or update an old one) opens in Olympus's own window, for you to
  edit and send yourself. The click sends nothing.
- **Ask for a bug report** (the author alone, on a player running 1.1.2 or newer): their addon
  opens a window of its own, never a game popup, saying the author asks for their Olympus bug
  report, with **See what is sent** (the exact text, the same as `/oly bug`), **Send** and **Not
  now**. Send goes to him alone, in game; Not now sends nothing; an ask from anyone else is
  ignored. On his side the report he asked for opens by itself in a window you can copy from (the
  sender and time on top, **Select all**), and stays in the Workshop's list; chat gets one short
  line. A report nobody asked for gets its line and the list only. Since 1.1.5 his addon keeps the
  last 30 reports in its saved variables: where the game loads those back, a logout or a `/reload`
  loses none, and his list opens them in the same window, the date on top for one from an earlier
  day. The Forever beta, which forgets addon data at every login, still loses them at each logout
  or `/reload`. No other player's addon keeps any, and the Workshop's copy for Discord says only
  how many came, never who sent them or what they say. His version checks and his
  `/oly status` open in copy windows too. A window that opens by itself takes no keyboard, waits
  until a fight is over, and never covers a report he is reading.
- In a dungeon, a raid or a match the game holds addon messages: the lines that send show greyed
  and say why. Not on yourself, enemies, offline names or Battle.net friends, and only while you
  are in an Olympus guild. It uses the game's own way for addons to add to its menus (a client
  without it gets no lines); no Blizzard function is replaced, and nothing opens the game's chat
  box.

**Olympus's own lines (1.2.5.1).** The profile, **Report to Olympus**, the Arena's lines and the
Church's show only for a player your client knows to be in an Olympus guild: the guild the game
gives for that player, your guild's roster, your last /who, his line on the Olympus channel this
session, the guild his own Olympus messages spoke for, or the signed leadership list. Opening a menu still sends nothing to find out. The version
lines and **Tell them about Olympus** show for anyone, and the Olympus window's own rows keep every
line. None of it shows before you accepted the Olympus Accord.

releases.name: Olympus 1.6.4
releases.notes:
Olympus 1.6.4

- Keeps the Chat tab visible while local approval or guild roster information is missing, with an explanation and the existing access checks.
- Retries installation of the offline-player message filter after a native API error. Manual-whisper errors remain visible.
- Defers Slayer congratulations during combat and instances, preserving unread letters and the idle-client event budget.
- Lets you turn recruiting off even after losing invite permission, and preserves that choice after login or permission recovery.
- Rechecks locally known guild removals and revocations before a join request. Shows up to eight contacts per guild so other guild choices stay accessible.

Close and reopen WoW after updating. Existing signed lists and guild approvals are preserved. Some realm-identification, missing-role and cross-guild delivery reports remain under investigation; this update does not guarantee synchronized live totals.

Validation: full repository checks passed, 5,548 tests / 0 failures. Real-client behavior is not implied by the offline results.

releases.name: Olympus 1.6.3
releases.notes:
Olympus 1.6.3

- Personal Discord verification is now at the top of The Realm, with clearer steps and one code-entry popup. Local delivery is kept separate from Discord access.
- Existing guild approvals control shared-tool participation across groups, professions, position sharing, layer help and games. Census and approval recovery remain available.
- Adds scoped, time-limited signed federation decisions, pardons, revocation and recovery for authorized staff.
- Contribution review can recognize settled gold mail and retained game history. Existing balances, anonymous defaults and consent are preserved.
- An authorized Treasurer can publish and withdraw up to four informational milestones.
- Improves Australian realm identification and prevents repeated realm-link recovery.
- Adds Akafoxslayer Thunderfury’s supplied portrait dragon and matching chat icon, with corrected portrait geometry. This is cosmetic and grants no rank.

Close and reopen WoW after updating, because this version adds addon files. Keep your SavedVariables.

Automatic guild-verification warnings remain paused. Private Olympus Link, automatic website feeds and Army QR activation are separate and are not enabled by this addon release. Report remaining issues with /oly bug.

releases.name: Olympus 1.6.2
releases.notes:
- Restores Forever realm identification after the game update, allowing retained role lists, role tabs and the correct census to load again.
- Uses existing High Council guild approvals for shared tools and Church conversion tracking, without another enrollment list. Eligible guilds outside Olympus Prime use voluntary contributions.
- Pauses automatic guild verification warnings, including guild-master reminders. Manual verification and resending remain available.

Close and reopen WoW after updating. If a role or tab is still missing, please send an `/oly bug` report.

releases.name: Olympus 1.6.1
releases.notes:
The Realm can show guild masters and officers together again. Use **Show → Guild Masters & Officers** above the guild list. Older roster observations show their age. Guilds without roster details show that leadership is unknown.

This update lays the groundwork for signed guild enrollment, recruiting handoffs, Church conversion rankings and fugitive decisions. These tools become available through a separate rollout.

Close and reopen WoW after updating. If something still fails, use `/oly bug`.
